description: Application identity per platform. This is spec data, not documentation, because automation needs it: a device flow must verify which app is in the foreground before it concludes anything, and force-stop the right package before relaunching with new arguments.

The side-by-side cost is accepted: a device holds one of the two at a time, so a device flow installs one at a time. Do not treat this as a blocker and do not open a rename against the SDK repo.

sharedLibraryIdentity.comment: sample-ui is a library, so it never carries an application identity. It must also never READ one: the same library runs under eight different identities (these four, plus the four development samples in the SDK repos).

reserved.comment: Held by the development samples inside the SDK repos. The first two are CONTESTED: this repository's Flutter and Expo apps are specified to take them. SUPERSEDED BY THE 2026-09-17 RULING: the rename is SKIPPED, not deferred, and the first two ids are SHARED with the SDK repos' development samples rather than moved. The com.usesmileid.devsample.* root is no longer planned. Do not claim, reuse, or nest under the rest.
reserved.com.usesmileid.sample.flutter: SHARED, rename SKIPPED — flutter SDK repo sample, both platforms; referenced by its E2E workflow. Per the 2026-09-17 ruling it keeps this id and so does this repository's Flutter app, so the two cannot be installed side by side and a device run installs one at a time
reserved.com.usesmileid.sample.expo: SHARED, rename SKIPPED — react-native-expo SDK repo Expo sample, both platforms. Per the 2026-09-17 ruling it keeps this id and so does this repository's Expo app, so the two cannot be installed side by side and a device run installs one at a time
reserved.com.usesmileid.sample: android SDK repo sample (+.debug) and iOS SDK repo sample; referenced by both repos' E2E workflows. Not contested — this repository's apps sit one level below it
reserved.com.usesmileid.sample.react: react-native-expo SDK repo bare-RN sample (iOS side reads com.usesmileid.sample.rn). Not contested
reserved.usesmileid-sample: URL scheme claimed by the Expo development sample

rationale: DECIDED 2026-08-28: one id family, com.usesmileid.sample.*, for all four apps. This SUPERSEDES the original com.usesmileid.sampleapps root, which was chosen to avoid the development samples entirely. Android moved first because it is the app reaching a store; iOS follows in its port. The cost is recorded rather than hidden: com.usesmileid.sample.flutter and com.usesmileid.sample.expo are held today by SDK-repo development samples, so those two SDK repos owe a rename before this repository's Flutter and Expo apps can be built. Both are unbuilt, so the debt is payable before it is due. Android and iOS collide with nothing.

What the superseded reasoning got right, and still applies to iOS: on iOS a bundle id nested under another app's id is the convention for app extensions, so com.usesmileid.sample.ios can read as an extension of the development sample com.usesmileid.sample. It is not a technical block — provisioning profiles are explicit — but expect it to look odd in the portal, and do not let anyone 'fix' it by nesting deeper.

Every id is distinct per platform because a single device can host three of these four apps at once, plus their development counterparts. Ids that collide cannot be installed side by side, which is exactly the comparison these apps exist to enable.

URL schemes are per app for the same reason: two apps claiming one scheme means a disambiguation prompt on Android and last-installed-wins on iOS, both of which break automation silently. The schemes are unchanged by the id move — they were never under the id root.

That collision also applies WITHIN one app, across its build types: debugSuffix separates the application ids, but the URL scheme is declared in the shared manifest, so a debug and a release build of the same app both claim it. CONFIRMED ON A DEVICE 2026-08-13: with both variants installed, opening usesmileid-sample-android://settings resolves to android/com.android.internal.app.ResolverActivity rather than to either app. A deep link raises a chooser and automation hangs on a dialog no flow asserts — the same silent failure as two apps sharing a scheme, from a source that looks harmless. Install one variant at a time, which is why the Maestro invocation names APP_ID explicitly rather than defaulting. Suffixing the scheme per build type was considered and rejected: the scheme is spec data shared by four apps and their flows, and per-variant schemes would fork it.

On a device, the word 'Sample' in the label means the registry-consuming app from this repository; a label without it is a development harness from an SDK repo. SUPERSEDED FOR iOS 2026-09-13, see the next entry.

DECIDED 2026-09-13: the iOS app's launcher label and App Store name are 'Smile ID' — the product's name, as a partner searches for it — and the store listing ships under it. Android, Flutter and Expo keep 'UseSmileID Sample' until each renames after the iOS release, so displayNameFamily is unchanged for now. This inverts the label heuristic above on iOS: the registry-consuming app is the one named for the product, and the SDK repo's development harness is the one labelled 'UseSmileID'. The v11 sample is also labelled 'Smile ID', so a tester holding both sees two identical labels — a known cost of the ruling, not an oversight.

DECIDED 2026-09-14: Android follows iOS — launcher label 'Smile ID', Play title 'Smile ID', and the shared description's first sentence, so the two listings read as one product again; the Settings footer moved with it to 'Smile ID · <version>' (screens.json appNameCopy records the chain). displayNameFamily stays 'UseSmileID Sample' for Flutter and Expo until their ports rename. The label heuristic above is now inverted on Android too: the app named for the product is this repository's, and 'UseSmileID' marks an SDK repo's development harness.

DECIDED 2026-09-17: the identifier rename in the Flutter and react-native-expo SDK repositories is SKIPPED, not deferred. This repository's Flutter and Expo apps take com.usesmileid.sample.flutter and com.usesmileid.sample.expo as they stand, sharing each id with that SDK repo's own development sample. This REVERSES the 2026-08-28 expectation that the rename would land as part of porting sample-ui to the four SDKs, and retires the com.usesmileid.devsample.* root that entry planned. The accepted cost is that a device cannot hold both apps at once, so a device flow installs one at a time and a run that needs the other uninstalls first. The benefit is that neither port waits on another repository to merge a rename before it can be built, which is why the cost was taken. Nobody should treat either id as blocked or open a rename against an SDK repo for it.
